newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's FMC boosted by U.S. health care changes.
newsitem.headline: Germany's FMC boosted by U.S. health care changes.

text.p: German medical services group Fresenius Medical Care AG said on Friday that changes in U.S. legislation governing home health care could significantly boost its earnings in the U.S.

A spokesman for the company said in response to a Reuters query that Fresenius could earn approximately $60 million more per year from the legal change, but warned that accurate estimates were not yet available.
On August 5, U.S. President Bill Clinton changed legislation governing private insurance payouts for home care for patients, the spokesman said.

While previously a patient received private insurance cover for 21 months, after which the state would pay contributions, the cut-off point for a move to state care had been raised to 30 months, meaning that Fresenius stood to sell more products in the U.S.
The average state payout per home care treatment was $126, while the average payout per treatment from private insurers is $250 per treatment, the spokesman said.
Shares in Fresenius Medical Care were up 1.95 percent at 151.90 marks in late electronic trade on Friday, compared to the overall market which was down around two percent at 4,339.52 points.
Fresenius Medical Care was created in September 1996 when German medical products group Fresenius AG merged its dialysis business with National Medical Care, a unit of U.S. group W.R. Grace.
